content_voiceover: This slide quantifies the clinical impact of extended half-life products, and the asymmetry between factor eight and factor nine is a classic board point. Extended half-life FVIII products only achieve a modest one-point-five to one-point-seven fold increase in half-life, translating to about a thirty percent reduction in annual infusions, with trough levels reaching just two to three percent, enough to shift severe hemophilia A toward a moderate phenotype. Extended half-life FIX products do dramatically better, four to six fold increase in half-life, a sixty percent reduction in infusion frequency, and troughs reaching five percent, enough to convert severe hemophilia B to a mild phenotype. The reason for this disparity is that factor eight's half-life is inherently capped by its obligate binding to von Willebrand factor, while factor nine has no such binding partner constraining it, so PEGylation or Fc-fusion technology has much more room to extend its circulation time.
keypoints: EHL FVIII: only 1.5-1.7 fold half-life increase, ~30% fewer infusions, trough 2-3%
EHL FIX: 4-6 fold half-life increase, ~60% fewer infusions, trough 5%
FVIII severe disease shifts to moderate phenotype; FIX severe shifts to mild phenotype
FVIII's VWF-binding dependence caps its achievable half-life extension
keypoint_voiceover: Extended half-life FVIII gains only one-point-five to one-point-seven fold, capped by its VWF binding, shifting severe disease to moderate. Extended half-life FIX gains four to six fold, unconstrained by VWF, shifting severe disease all the way to a mild phenotype.
